text: The contract end has no published REST operation, so the act arrives as a Temporal command on the partner's InstructionWorkflow execution on task queue rwb-partner, and its effect is read through GET /partners and GET /partner/instructions on base /api/recovery/partner/v1.
why: The Ownership Map gives S9 exactly six operations and none of them ends a contract, while TSD S9 T-A.2 gives each of the six a purpose that is the issue, the read, the acceptance, the invoice or the result of an instruction. Inventing a seventh operation would break the ownership rule and the plan's own contract; naming a workflow command as the entry point keeps the act inside the service that owns the partner and lets the screens read the effect on the two published reads.

text: An instruction is open when its status is SENT, ACCEPTED or IN_PROGRESS; DONE, DECLINED and RECALLED are not recalled. The recall is carried by partner_instruction.status with the published value RECALLED and the exit by partner.panel_status with EXITED, so this key adds no table, no column and no state value, and partner_user is neither read nor written because TSD S9 T3.1 gives it no field list. The contract end runs on the partner's InstructionWorkflow execution, which holds that partner's open instructions, because a contract end spans an instruction set and the sources fix the workflow's name only.
why: TSD S9 T3.2 gives a closed list of six instruction statuses and four panel statuses, and the sources never define which of them a recall enumerates, so a builder has to choose a set and mark it as an assumption rather than invent a new status. A recall flag or a re-selection column would change two tables three other stories of the service already write, need a DB story and break the additive rule of a published contract.

text: The re-selection of an affected case is a Temporal command from the contractEnd branch to rwb-case, one command per case, under R-UNI-45; this service writes no case row, moves no case state and holds no timer, and the command's name and answer shape are Not specified in the source documents (CG-B2-S9-013-1; ASM-B2-S9-013-3).
why: R-UNI-45's to_state is ROUTE_D6_REOPEN, a route state of the case, and TSD S9 T4 says the module has no case state machine of its own and acts on events from P3. The case, its route state and its timer rows are P3's, so the recall cannot be completed inside rwb-partner, and the alternatives — a REST call from a business step or a new event — are both rejected by the call-type rule and by the event set the service owns.

text: The contract end is idempotent per partner and end date: one entry, one recall set and one clock, a repeat answers the entry already written, and no event is published or consumed because EV-20 InstructionIssued and EV-21 PartnerResultSubmitted belong to the instruction stories.
why: The service owns exactly two events and both report the issue of an instruction and the result the partner records, so publishing either on a contract end would report a business fact that did not happen.
